newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kudu gas development takes a step forward.
newsitem.headline: Kudu gas development takes a step forward.

text.p: Shell Exploration and Production Namibia BV said on Wednesday it had applied for the declaration of a petroleum field for all of the Kudu gas field licence area in a major step forward in its development.
Shell is operator and majority owner of the concession, with 75 percent, together with partners Texaco Inc (15 percent) and Energy Africa Ltd (10 percent).

The company said in a statement that a recently-completed comprehensive field review demonstrated that sufficient gas was present in the area covered by a 1993 3D seismic survey for an initial development to supply the Namibian market.
"Development could start in a part of the Kudu field area containing gas volumes in place of 1.8 trillion cubic feet (tcf)," Shell said in a statement received here.

"A similar volume is expected in the remainder of the field area, while further scope for volumes in place in excess of five tcf are estimated in the remainder of the Kudu Licence Area covering more than 5,000 square km."

Present volumes are estimated to be more than sufficient for an initial development of the Kudu gas field to supply a 700 MW power station. Such a power plant would make Namibia self-sufficient in power for the foreseeable future, allowing also for export of electricity.

"Further detailed studies and engineering data collection are being initiated together with concurrent discussions and negotiations to secure the market with the intention to reach a final investment decision in 1998," Shell said.
First gas could be brought to shore in late 2000 with generation in early 2001.
Total cost of the initial development of the project is estimated at more than $300 million, excluding the cost of power generation.
Shell said it was also considering a second phase aimed at a large gas export scheme for the supply of gas to power and industrial markets in South Africa.
Further exploratory appraisal drilling is planned to prove the additional gas necessary for the next development phase with preparations in hand to enable drilling to start in the first half of 1998.
